title: Mississauga's Mughal Mahal, Known for Amritsari Kulcha, Is Expanding to Brampton
excerpt: The Punjabi restaurant, trading in Mississauga since 1990, announced a Brampton location on social media. No opening date has been set.
body:
• Mughal Mahal, the Mississauga Punjabi restaurant known for Amritsari kulcha, is opening a second location in Brampton, it announced on social media.
  • No opening date has been announced. The restaurant says the Brampton site is "coming soon," with "the ribbon up and the tandoor hot."
  • The Brampton menu will match the original: tandoor-baked kulchas, chole and thalis.
  • The original at 7071 Airport Road, Mississauga, has traded since 1990, according to the restaurant.

Brampton residents who drive to Mississauga for Amritsari kulcha will soon have a shorter trip. Mughal Mahal, a Punjabi restaurant in Mississauga, is opening a new location in Brampton, according to insauga.com's report of the restaurant's social media announcement.

"Same flavours. New location. Zero compromises," the restaurant said in its announcement, adding that "the ribbon is up and the tandoor is hot." No opening date has been announced.

What Will Be on the Menu

Mughal Mahal specialises in Amritsari kulcha, the stuffed, buttered flatbread from Amritsar in Punjab, baked in a tandoor and usually served with chole, or spiced chickpeas. The Brampton location will serve the same menu as the original, including fresh tandoor kulchas, chole and thalis, the traditional platters that combine several dishes in one meal, according to the report.

The restaurant's own site describes a from-scratch kitchen and lists the Amritsari kulcha with channa among its signature plates at its Mississauga address, 7071 Airport Road. Diaspora readers in Peel Region can use that site for the original location's hours and menu while the Brampton opening date is pending.

"Zero compromises," the restaurant said in its announcement, adding that "the ribbon is up and the tandoor is hot." No opening date has been announced."

More Than Three Decades in Mississauga

According to its website, Mughal Mahal has been serving Indian food since 1990. It says its commitment to "real Indian food has remained unwavering" over that time, and that it uses Himalayan herbs and more than 30 spices in its curries. "If you've been driving to Mississauga for it, your drive just got shorter," the restaurant told fans.

A Growing Brampton Food Scene

The opening adds to Brampton's South Asian food scene, where Punjabi restaurants are among the city's most popular spots and where a large Punjabi diaspora sustains demand for regional dishes such as kulcha-chole. Until an opening date and Brampton address are confirmed, the Mississauga original remains the place to get the dish the new site promises to replicate.
